newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norway forecasts oil investment up 20 pct in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Norway forecasts oil investment up 20 pct in 1997.

text.p: Oil investment on the Norwegian continental shelf will be around 55 billion crowns ($7.9 billion) in 1997, up 8.8 billion crowns from 1996, the government department Statistics Norway (SSB) said on Thursday.
In a first quarter report on petroleum activities, the SSB attributed the increase mainly to higher investment in field development and in fields already producing.
In 1996, investment in oil and gas production and pipeline transportation systems amounted to 46 billion crowns -- the lowest level since 1991.
SSB said it expected oil companies to spend 28.2 billion crowns in field development this year, while investment in fields already in production was forecast to hit a record high 10.1 billion crowns.

It said exploration spending was seen reaching 7.5 billion crowns, up 1.8 billion from the year ago figure. Land-based investment was projected to amount to one billion crowns, the lowest level since 1989.
